title: Frontier meet-rigidity is completion-relative, not universal
carrier: K_{2,3}^{0,U} = {0, f1,f2, g1,g2,g3, U}; 0<all<U; f_i<g_j for all i,j
question: Is Thm 120a (distinct upper-frontier g,g' meet to w) a MacNeille artifact or a completion-universal law?

macneille.note: = canonical extension L^delta (finite poset: all filters/ideals principal)

ideal_downset_D(L).note: meets = intersection of downsets; g_i^g_j = downset {0,f1,f2} = w. Meet-rigid. The 6 new elements are the free JOINS g_i v g_j = {0,f1,f2,g_i,g_j} < U (empty set as new bottom, w, d12,d13,d23,d123): join-rigidity of the DUAL (coatom) frontier is what breaks here, not w's meet frontier.

filter_upset_F(L).note: order-dual construction (reverse inclusion of upsets); meet = union of upsets. g_i^g_j = up(g_i) U up(g_j) = {g_i,g_j,U} = z_ij, THREE distinct NEW elements strictly above w = up(f1)^up(f2) = {g1,g2,g3,U}. Only the full triple meets to w => H_min(w) 3-uniform, mu(w)=3=|G|. Cor 120b freezing (mu=2) BROKEN.

theorems.121a: Frontier meet-rigidity (Thm 120a) is NOT completion-universal. It holds in MacNeille and in the ideal/downset completion, but FAILS in the filter/upset completion, where the upper frontier G of w carries the FREE meet-semilattice structure: pairwise meets g_i^g_j are distinct new elements > w, so H_min(w) = {G} is |G|-uniform and mu(w)=|G|.
theorems.121b: For finite posets MacNeille = canonical extension (every filter is a down-directed upset = principal, dually for ideals), so both freeze mu=2. The freezing is exactly the consequence of SIMULTANEOUS join- and meet-density: MacNeille is the unique dense completion in which L is both join- and meet-dense.
theorems.121c: One-sided completions unfreeze exactly one frontier: the downset completion D(L) (join-dense only) keeps meet-rigidity of w but unfreezes the DUAL join-frontier (adjoining free joins g_i v g_j < U); the upset completion F(L) (meet-dense only) unfreezes w's meet-frontier to mu(w)=|G|. For K_{n,m}^{0,U}: filter completion gives mu(w)=m; ideal completion keeps mu(w)=2 but the dual (coatom-below-U) join-multiplicity becomes n. So the Pass-120 realization NEGATIVE (K_n only) is a MacNeille/canonical phenomenon; over F(L) the |G|-uniform hyperedge IS realized.
theorems.121d_arith: DUAL join-rigidity reading (boxt = neg Box): in MacNeille the lower frontier F of w is a family of consistency-like sentences whose pairwise joins collapse to the Henkin cut w (any two already generate the phantom limit). This collapse is NOT order-forced: the free downset completion keeps such joins distinct. Hence 'pairwise joins of Con^orb iterates generate the phantom limit' is a property of BOTH-density (Lindenbaum/MacNeille), not of the bare consistency order -- partial reading of the Pass-69 Con^orb tower question; exact identification left open.
